audit.whatIsWrong: Five of the seven level-chart rows disagreed with their own why[] text and with the packet chart.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Sett, Sett, Illaoi, Illaoi, Illaoi, Illaoi, Skill. On disk rows 0 and 1 read Skill/Illaoi while whys[0] ('Sett's punch passive and grit shield out-trade your Level 1') and whys[1] ('At Level 2 his Haymaker true damage still wins the short trade') both give those levels to Sett; rows 3 and 4 read Skill while whys[3] and whys[4] give them to Illaoi; row 6 read Illaoi while whys[6] and the late block both call it a coinflip. EVEN 6/10 at 54.49% over 2081 games is right — the rows were simply out of sync with the prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 1 to Sett, rows 3 and 4 to Illaoi, row 6 to Skill, in both layers as one atomic group. The chart now matches the packet and every why.

audit.why: Spikes at 3-5, 6, first item and late match the kits: Harsh Lesson (4s) online at 3, Leap of Faith at 6 (120/95/70s) against The Show Stopper (120/100/80s), and Sett's Grit-Haymaker staying relevant late because its centre is true damage.
audit.corrected: Kept; only the chart rows around them were fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is written as a flat 'E stun' (dosFull[2], dontsFull[1], report[11]) and Haymaker as a generic 'true-damage burst'.
audit.why: Riot on Facebreaker (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, 490 range): 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' For a solo laner that is the whole interaction — stay on one side of him and his only hard CC is a slow. Riot on Haymaker (W, 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s): he 'passively stores damage he takes as Grit', then spends it for a shield and a punch 'dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides'. So the page's own advice to poke him with Tentacles is what pays for the shield, and the centre-vs-sides split is dodgeable positioning that was never stated.
audit.corrected: One-side rule on Facebreaker written into dosFull[2] and report[5]; the Grit-feeds-shield loop and the centre/edge damage split written into dontsFull[0], report[5] and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Haymaker as matchup-defining with no number, and Facebreaker appeared in no cooldown text at all.
audit.why: Haymaker 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, Facebreaker 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Knuckle Down 9/8/7/6/5s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80s — against Test of Spirit at 16/15/14/13/12s. Haymaker at 18 seconds rank 1 is the longest lane cooldown either champion has and is the real window.
audit.corrected: Real numbers for Haymaker and Facebreaker written into the cooldown block.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling is already called for early. Sett's passive gives 'additional health regeneration based off of his missing health', so Grievous Wounds genuinely bites in a grind — the existing text is right.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — His shield + true-damage burst. Don’t fight into it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker (18s at rank 1): shield scales with the Grit your poke feeds him — its centre is true damage. - Facebreaker 16s: stuns only from both sides. - Test of Spirit 16s: never spend it on chip. - Leap of Faith: kill windows.

notes: UNVERIFIED and left alone: spikes[1].text and wants.foe[2] describe The Show Stopper as a suppression ('R-suppresses in', 'R suppression'). Riot's description in the kit file says only that Sett 'carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground' — whether it is a true suppression that beats Tenacity or cleanses is not in the local data, so neither the claim nor a correction was written. Same standing issue as the other Illaoi pages: her R carries derived 'grounding' and 'untargetable' flags and her E a 'slow' flag that Riot's descriptions do not support — nothing written on any of them.
